title: Minkä näköinen: asking about one person's or thing's appearance
summary: Minkä näköinen asks what one person or thing looks like. Minkä näköinen talo on? — Talo on korkea.
targetSkills: Minkä näköinen: asking about one person's or thing's appearance
prerequisiteSkills: Minkä väristä: asking the colour of a substance
objectives: Ask what one person or thing looks like with minkä näköinen.
Give a visible characteristic rather than an unrelated identity or character fact.

sections.title: Meaning and pattern
paragraphs: Singular refers to one person or one thing in these patterns.
The genitive is a relationship form; in these question phrases minkä means of what or which.
An adjective is a word that describes a quality.
Minkä näköinen asks what one person or thing looks like. It asks for visible appearance rather than every aspect of character or quality. Minkänäköinen is a standard joined spelling.
keyPoints: A fact such as being friendly does not by itself describe visible appearance.

sections.title: Answering the question
paragraphs: Answer with a visible characteristic in the basic adjective form: Talo on korkea (“The house is tall”). A short description such as Korkea is natural too. An appearance answer need not repeat näköinen when a direct adjective supplies the requested information.
A natural short reply to “Minkä näköinen talo on?” is “Korkea.” (“Tall.”). Use the full reply when it makes the person, action or correction clearer.
A visible colour can answer an appearance question. Reject the incorrect visual description before supplying the actual appearance; the complete negative phrase is provided.
The exercises show supporting Finnish words and their meanings when recalling them is not the task. Read the complete English meaning before choosing the question or answer form.
keyPoints: Give the requested visible characteristic using the singular describing form.
